first.rationale: Two of the three pressures (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) are internal funnel problems, and the inherited record points the same way twice from independent sessions: memory_86 (shorter onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields produced durable SMB activation lift). Convergent, unflagged evidence aimed directly at the observed regressions is the best single-slot bet for sustainable qualified revenue. I am spending verification on memory_73 and memory_86 rather than on the two I already trust most cheaply. memory_73 is the memory the situation most tempts me toward — the competitor's entry pricing makes promotional pricing feel like the obvious counter — and it is the one memory carrying an explicit defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of which accounts landed in which bucket. A discount program justified by a possibly-inflated effect is exactly the kind of move that books revenue now and degrades revenue quality later, so I want the original record before I either act on it or set it aside. I verify memory_86 because it is the memory I actually intend to act on; the honest asymmetry is that I should scrutinize my chosen path at least as hard as the one I am declining. Open uncertainties I am not resolving with this pull: memories 86 and 31 were consolidated on days 52 and 12, before the current QoQ decline, so the decline may have a cause (traffic mix, competitor-driven change in who is signing up) that onboarding length does not touch — in which case a null result is informative rather than a failure. memory_91 (activation messaging) is a live alternative and could be the better slot if verification shows memory_86's lift was concentrated in a cohort unlike today's inflow. I am also flagging a value risk on my own choice, not just on pricing: shortening onboarding and cutting required fields can strip the qualification signal that makes revenue 'qualified,' so the experiment should measure downstream account quality and retention, not just completion and week-one activation. Standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the direction is well-corroborated but the corroboration predates the regression, and the failure mode is quiet quality erosion rather than a loud miss. If verification undercuts memory_86, I will reallocate the slot to activation_messaging rather than default to promotional_pricing.
